pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, The Red Vineyard — a whole hillside of vines burning red, orange and gold under a yellow evening sky, the rows laid in thick heavy strokes of scarlet and flame with small black stakes standing up among them, a band of blue green trees and a low blue ridge closing the far side, a yellow stubble field beyond the vines with a cart and a horse standing at the right, and all through the vineyard the pickers at their work, women in blue smocks and white caps bent low over the rows, one carrying a green parasol over her shoulder, another stooping with a basket of grapes in both hands, a man crouched among the leaves cutting bunches, and in the front a great blue tub set down in the vines with a wet track of violet and grey running away below it, i am the true vine, and my father is the keeper of the vineyard, …
pictures.name: pd_gogh_wijngaard

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, Old Woman Reading a Lectionary — one very old woman filling the picture in profile, lit softly out of a dim olive brown ground, her deeply lined face bent down over a great open book held up in both hands, her eyes lowered to the page and her mouth closed, a pale striped linen band wound round her head under a soft brown fur cap, a heavy dark blue cloak with a thick fur collar over her shoulders fastened at the throat with a small gold clasp set with a red stone, her two old worn hands spread over the edges of the leaves, and the big open pages catching all the light, printed in close black gothic columns with a little woodcut set into the text, remain in me, and i will remain in you, …
pictures.name: pd_dou_old_woman_reading_a_lectionary

pictures.scene: Peder Severin Kroyer, Midsummer Eve Bonfire on Skagen Beach — a great heap of dry brushwood and old timber burning on the sand at dusk, the flames torn sideways by the wind into a long tongue of white gold and orange that sweeps right across the upper half of the picture, sparks blowing off it and a deep blue violet evening sky behind, a man in a brown coat at the right thrusting a long pole into the fire while another in a pale summer suit and a straw hat laughs beside him, two women in long white dresses and wide flowered hats standing in the firelight, children running and dancing hand in hand round the burning pile, their shadows thrown out across the lit sand, and in the front a close row of onlookers with their backs to us, two young men in dark blue jerseys with their arms over each other's shoulders, a sailor in a flat cap, and women and children seated on the sand in dark hats and shawls watching the blaze, such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned, …
pictures.name: pd_kroyer_midsummer_eve_bonfire

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Harvesters — a great pear tree standing up through the whole height of the picture with its branches spread right across the top, a field of ripe wheat behind it cut into a wide gold lane of stubble with standing sheaves set up in cones, a reaper swinging his sickle in the standing corn, a woman stooping to bind an armful of ears, a man carrying his bundle away between the stooks, a scythe and a rake leaning against the trunk, a dark hedge, a far church spire and wooded hills beyond, and in the shade under the tree the harvest meal, a man sprawled flat on his back asleep in a white shirt with his mouth open, a man in a black hat biting into his bread, another tipping a brown jug up to drink, a woman in a white coif eating from a bowl with a spoon, a man in a straw hat and others in a wide black hat and blue jacket reaching to a dish, a loaf and a crock set out on a white cloth on the ground, and a basket of bread beside them, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be my disciples, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_harvesters

pictures.scene: Solomon Alexander Hart, The Feast of the Rejoicing of the Law at the Synagogue in Leghorn — the inside of an old synagogue with worked stone arches springing across the top of the picture and two great silver lamps hanging on long chains from them, a white carved marble gallery rail running across the middle hung with an embroidered cloth worked in flowers, tall branched candlesticks burning behind it and bearded elders in prayer shawls and fur trimmed hats leaning over the rail with women and children beside them looking down, and in front a procession carrying the scrolls of the law, a man in a wide black hat and a long striped prayer shawl holding a scroll in a crimson velvet mantle hugged against his breast with its silver bells and crowns showing above it, another behind him carrying a scroll dressed in blue, more men in red caps, green and brown coats and turbans crowding in at the left, an old man in a scarlet robe seated at a dark carved desk at the right, and the pale stone floor of the hall running away below them, so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be complete, …
pictures.name: pd_hart_rejoicing_of_the_law

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Carrying the Cross — one tall figure of Christ filling the whole picture against a deep blue green ground streaked with pale cloud, the great raw wooden cross laid up over His right shoulder and running from the bottom of the frame out through the top corner, its grain and knots lit along the edges, His face turned up and lit from above with the eyes raised and brimming, a crown of long thorns pressed down over His brow with small drops of blood running from it down the temple and into His dark beard, a deep blue green mantle wrapped heavily round His shoulders and falling in broad folds down the whole left side, a brilliant crimson robe showing at the throat and along the arm, the neck of it open a little over the upper chest, and both long pale hands closed gently round the beam, the upper one laid flat against the wood with the fingers spread and the lower one hanging open below it, held not as a weight dragged but as a thing embraced, greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Supper at Emmaus — a great dark stone hall with a huge round arch carried up over the whole upper half of the picture, worked courses of pale brown masonry at either side and a tall pier at the right, and under it a small round table pushed against the wall covered with a brilliant white cloth that is the brightest thing in the room, pewter plates, a glass, a knife and a folded napkin set out on it, a heavy gold fringed carpet hanging over the near side, and seated behind it Christ in a pale rose robe with a grey mantle fallen across His knees, His long hair loose on His shoulders and a soft blaze of light standing out all round His head, His face turned quietly out and both hands holding a broken loaf over the plate, at the left a young disciple in a dark red jacket swung round on his chair with his hands caught up at his chin staring at Him, at the right an older man in a worn brown coat leaning across the table with his mouth open and his hand flat on the cloth, and behind them a serving boy in a dark coat stooping in with a dish of meat held out on a plate, no longer do i call you servants, but i have called you friends, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_supper_at_emmaus

pictures.scene: Jean Francois Millet, The Sower — one enormous peasant striding down a ploughed hillside at dusk, his whole figure crossing the picture from the bottom of the frame up into the pale grey evening sky, a battered soft hat pulled down over his face so that the brow and cheek are in shadow, a worn red brown jacket with the sleeves full, a blue smock showing under it and heavy blue trousers bound at the knee, his legs wrapped round and round with rags and straw and his feet sunk in the broken earth, a coarse white seed bag slung across his chest and held open against his hip in one fist, the other arm swung wide out of the left of the picture at the top of its throw with the seed flying from the open hand, the dark brown field running away under him in long furrows and clods, a strip of bare hillside behind with a yoke of oxen and a ploughman small against the skyline, a warm bar of sunset light low on the right and birds dropping to the ground behind him, i appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will remain, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sower

pictures.scene: Jean Leon Gerome, The Christian Martyrs' Last Prayer — the floor of a Roman amphitheatre seen from the sand, a great dark maned lion standing out alone in the middle of the picture with his head lowered and turned to the side, his heavy shoulders and mane thrown up black against the pale ground and his broad paws set in the raked sand, the long curved wall of the arena running right across behind him with its low barrier, a carved stone gateway with green bronze doors shut in the middle, tall pitch torches burning on poles along the wall with black smoke blowing off them, and above that tier on tier of seats packed with thousands of tiny spectators crowding the arcades and the colonnade along the top, a dark storm sky with grey and cream cloud rolled across the upper part of the picture, the corner of a great building and a gilt statue with a spear showing over the roofline at the right, and the empty raked sand running away in long pale sweeps below, if the world hates you, understand that it hated me first, …
pictures.name: pd_gerome_martyrs

pictures.scene: Valentin de Boulegne, Saint Paul Writing His Epistles — one large figure bent low over a writing table, lit out of a deep brown ground that goes almost black above him, his high bald forehead creased in three long furrows and a heavy russet beard spread over his chest, his eyes lowered and his mouth half open as he thinks out the next word, long brown hair falling at the side of his head, a dark green robe with the sleeve pushed up the forearm and a brilliant vermilion cloak gathered over his shoulder and falling in great folds over the front of the table, his right hand reaching across with a white quill just dipped and a small round ink pot standing under it, a big open book propped before him with a loose written sheet laid across the page, a second book lying open at the left with a pair of spectacles set down on it, a penknife and a little pile of cut quills on the bare plank beside them, and the white pages taking all the light in the picture, no servant is greater than his master, if they persecuted me, they will persecute you as well, …
pictures.name: pd_valentin_paul

pictures.scene: Enrique Simonet, Flevit super illam — Christ standing on a bare rocky shoulder of the Mount of Olives at evening, a tall full length figure in a long dark blue robe seen in profile with his long hair falling loose, one arm stretched right out over the valley and the hand opened toward the city, the other lifted behind it, his face turned down toward Jerusalem and his sandalled feet set on the stone, two companions close behind him, one in a long cream mantle with a white headcloth wrapped round his head and his hands folded, bowed and looking where he points, another beside him with a grey beard and a striped headcloth in a dark blue cloak stretching his arm out the same way, more figures crowded in at the left edge of the picture, and below them the whole valley lying grey and dim with scattered white houses, dark olive groves and the long pale platform of the temple catching the last light, a bar of cloud along the horizon, a pale rose sky above it with a small white star, the sun sinking as a hazy disc behind the hills, and in front a worked slope of broken limestone with dark thistles and scrub, if i had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin, …
pictures.name: pd_simonet_flevit

pictures.scene: Jorg Breu the Elder, The Crowd Crying Out Against Him — a close press of a dozen heads crowded up against a stone step, every face turned the same way and shouting, in the front a heavy set priest in a tall white mitre sewn with gold and green jewels, a pale yellow cope fringed with gold over a deep green robe and a long crimson brocaded sleeve, both hands lifted with the fingers spread as he argues, a second man bent toward him in a black cap and a wide white fur collar over a scarlet gown with black and gold embroidered sleeves, his mouth open and a small rolled paper held out in his fist, a dark bearded man in a jewelled gold mitre at the right staring up open mouthed, behind them a man in a green and black cap bellowing, another in a white turban, a thin man with his head thrown back and his jaw dropped, heads in red hoods and black caps packed in behind, bare arms and hands thrown up above them all at the top of the picture, a plain dark wall at the left and the pale stone of the steps running across the bottom corner, they hated me without reason, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Saint Peter Preaching — a pale crazed fresco of an old apostle standing out at the left of the picture, Peter in a soft blue tunic with a great golden orange mantle wrapped round him and falling to his bare feet, a thin gold halo behind his white hair and short white beard, his head turned and his mouth open in speech, one hand lifted with two fingers raised and the other gathering the heavy cloth at his hip, a young man in a blue gown and a dark green cap standing close behind his shoulder with more faces crowded beyond him, and in front of him the listeners pressed together, a young woman kneeling in a dark blue mantle with a white headband and her face lifted, another leaning her cheek on her hand beside her, an old man kneeling in a rose red cloak with his white bearded head bowed right down, ranks of men behind them in blue caps, brown hoods and bare heads all turned toward the speaker, two friars in white habits and dark mantles standing at the right edge, a green wooded mountain with small dark trees rising across the whole top of the picture and a band of plain plaster at the side, and you also must testify, because you have been with me from the beginning, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_saint_peter_preaching

lines.text: I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard. He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.
You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.
I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing.
If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
This is to My Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.
As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.
If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father's commandments and remain in His love.
I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
You are My friends if you do what I command you.
No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.
You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
This is My command to you: Love one another.
If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first.
If you were of the world, it would love you as its own. Instead, the world hates you, because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.
Remember the word that I spoke to you: No servant is greater than his master. If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
But they will treat you like this because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father.
But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: They hated Me without reason.
When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, He will testify about Me.
And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.
